subject: MAP milestone: Technical gating — benchmarks, owners, and model shortlist
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@healthsentry.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@healthsentry.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: post-call technical milestone - draft attached

Hi Amit, Priya —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Per our discussion I’m attaching a first draft of the Mutual Action Plan focused on the technical evaluation milestone (attached as MAP-draft-v1.pdf). The doc captures the scope we talked through and the checkpoints we’ll need to unblock a production evaluation. High level:

- Target close date for the MAP: 2027-06-15 (customer target; flexible if E2E testing expands)
- Technical gating milestone (this thread): set up benchmark runs, agree on success criteria, shortlist candidate models, and confirm test dataset + telemetry access
- Dependencies: secure test data access, SOC2 evidence exchange, sandbox capacity for 48-hour load runs

Action items I captured from today’s call (proposed owners):
1) Provide benchmark template and initial model shortlist — Redwood (Marcus) — due 2027-04-26
2) Share sanitized test corpus & acceptance examples — HealthSentry (Amit/Priya) — due 2027-04-28
3) SOC2 / security checkpoint (questions & evidence) — HealthSentry to send; Redwood to provide controls doc — due 2027-04-29
4) Schedule 1-day benchmark run window & validate observability hooks — Redwood infra (Neha) — target week of 2027-05-10

Benchmarks we plan to propose (will formalize in the attached spreadsheet):
- Quality: pass rate on acceptance prompt set >= 92% (per task-specific rubric)
- Latency: P95 infer latency < 150ms for 512-token context (single-request, no batching) OR < 80ms with continuous batching profile (if accepted)
- Cost: incremental inference cost <= $0.80 per 1k tokens for production-like profile (goal)
- Stability: <1.5% variance in token rate across a 24-hour run

Next steps for this week: Marcus will send the benchmark template + shortlist and I’ll update the MAP with assigned owners. Can you confirm the test dataset timeline and whether you can share the SOC2 questionnaire you mentioned?

Attachments: MAP-draft-v1.pdf, benchmark-template-v2.xlsx

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0148
From: Amit Shah <amit@healthsentry.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@healthsentry.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 18:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: post-call technical milestone - draft attached

Kimberly —

Appreciate the clear recap and the draft. A few quick notes from our side after debriefing with the engineering team:

- Latency target: we’d be more comfortable if the P95 target for single-request is capped at 120ms (we run a fairly latency-sensitive UI path). If you can show a batching path that achieves sub-80ms for our typical traffic shape, that’s attractive but we’ll need to validate UX impact.
- Cost: the $0.80/1k token looks reasonable as a starting goal — please include a sensitivity row in the workbook showing 0.6/0.8/1.0 $/1k tokens.
- Model shortlist: please include a couple of open-source candidates and one commercially optimized model. We want to see a breadth of trade-offs.
- SOC2: attached is a sanitized copy of the questionnaire we run for vendors (SOC2-request-answers.pdf) — we expect Redwood to indicate where you can provide evidence and where we’ll accept attestations.

We can share the sanitized test corpus by 2027-04-28 as proposed. Also request that you include an explicit acceptance rubric for the top-line quality metric (how pass rate is calculated and examples of failures).

Can we lock the benchmark run for the week of 2027-05-10? Our infra team will be available then but would like a confirmed 24-hour window so we can schedule on-call rotations.

Thanks — looking forward to Marcus’s template.

—Amit
Amit Shah
Head of Product Engineering | HealthSentry
amit@healthsentry.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit@healthsentry.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@healthsentry.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: post-call technical milestone - draft attached

Thanks Amit — agreed on the adjustments. I’ve updated the milestone checklist below and assigned owners / target dates. I’ll also push an updated MAP (v1.1) to the Drive link.

Updated technical gating milestone (concise):
- Objective: validate model(s) that meet HealthSentry quality, latency, and cost thresholds for the customer-facing assistant path.

Acceptance criteria (numeric):
- Quality: task pass rate >= 92% on the acceptance prompt set (rubric attached in workbook). Failure modes documented and sample outputs included.
- Latency: P95 single-request <= 120ms at 512-token context; P95 with Redwood continuous-batching profile <= 80ms (if customer enables batching).
- Cost: median inference cost <= $0.85 per 1k tokens across the candidate model shortlist (sensitivity included at 0.6/0.85/1.0).
- Reliability: <2% error rate and <2% throughput variance during a 24-hour production-like run.

Model shortlist (initial candidates) — Marcus to validate performance profiles and provide exact model IDs in the workbook:
- Llama-2-13b-chat (quantized) — open-source baseline
- Mistral-Instruct-7B — high-efficiency option
- Redwood-Instruct-4B-fp16 — Redwood-curated commercial variant for comparison

Owners & milestones: 
1) Marcus Lin — deliver benchmark-template-v2.xlsx + populate initial model IDs and expected latency/cost rows — due 2027-04-26
2) Amit/Priya (HealthSentry) — deliver sanitized test corpus + acceptance examples — due 2027-04-28
3) Kimberly — update MAP with owners and dependencies; coordinate schedule and sign-off — due 2027-04-27
4) Neha Kapoor (Redwood infra) — provision sandbox capacity, observability hooks, and schedule 24-hour run (target week of 2027-05-10). Confirm exact window by 2027-04-30

Dependencies / Risks:
- Data access: if HealthSentry cannot provide a representative corpus, we’ll need to run with synthetic proxies which may affect acceptance confidence.
- SOC2 evidence: gaps could delay commercial sign-off; we will flag attestations vs. documented evidence in the MAP.
- Model compatibility: if a shortlisted model lacks quantized kernels for the target infra, latency goals may not be achievable without additional engineering effort. Marcus will call out those cases.

I’ve attached the updated benchmark workbook and a short rubric page inside the sheet. Marcus — can you prioritize the model-ID pass and a quick expected-latency estimate so Amit’s team can review?

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
From: Priya Rao <priya.rao@healthsentry.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit@healthsentry.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: post-call technical milestone - draft attached

Kimberly / Marcus —

Thanks — this looks good and aligns with what our engineering leadership expects. Confirming:
- HealthSentry will deliver the sanitized corpus by 2027-04-28.
- We prefer the 24-hour run window the week of 2027-05-10; please propose specific slots by 2027-04-30 so we can lock shift coverage.
- We reviewed the model shortlist conceptually — please include the exact model artifact/package names and whether quantized variants will be used.

One ask: can Redwood include a short run with telemetry that surfaces per-request token breakdowns (tokenization time, model compute, networking) so we can attribute latency? That will be useful for our SRE team to identify optimization levers.

We’ll review MAP v1.1 once you post the update. Thanks for moving quickly on this.

—Priya
Priya Rao
Director, Platform Engineering | HealthSentry
